malpraxis-medical.description:
Medical malpractice (malpraxis medical) in Romania is primarily governed by Legea nr. 95/2006 privind reforma in domeniul sanatatii (Law no. 95/2006 on Healthcare Reform), specifically Title XVI on civil liability for medical personnel and healthcare providers, along with Legea nr. 46/2003 privind drepturile pacientului (Law no. 46/2003 on Patient Rights). Under Romanian law, medical malpractice occurs when a healthcare professional deviates from accepted medical standards, causing harm to a patient through negligence, incompetence, or failure to obtain informed consent.

Our firm handles a wide range of medical malpractice claims, including diagnostic errors and delayed diagnosis, surgical mistakes and post-operative complications, medication administration errors, negligence during pregnancy and childbirth, hospital-acquired infections, and failure to provide adequate informed consent as required under Art. 649-668 of Law 95/2006. We work with independent medical experts to evaluate the standard of care and establish the causal link between the medical act and the harm suffered.

For foreigners and English speakers navigating the Romanian healthcare system, legal representation is essential. Medical records, expert reports, and court proceedings are conducted entirely in Romanian. Our bilingual team ensures you fully understand your rights, the procedural steps, and the potential outcomes. We handle communication with hospitals, insurance companies, and the Colegiul Medicilor din Romania (Romanian College of Physicians), allowing you to focus on recovery while we pursue the compensation you deserve for material damages, lost income, and pain and suffering.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is the statute of limitations for medical malpractice claims in Romania?
faq.a1: Under Romanian civil law, the general statute of limitations for personal injury claims, including medical malpractice, is three years from the date the patient became aware (or should have become aware) of the harm and the identity of the responsible party. In some cases involving ongoing treatment or delayed discovery of the injury, this period may start later. It is essential to consult an attorney as soon as possible to ensure your claim is filed within the legal deadline.
faq.q2: How do I file a medical malpractice complaint in Romania?
faq.a2: The first step is typically to file a complaint with the Comisia de Monitorizare si Competenta Profesionala pentru Cazurile de Malpraxis (Monitoring and Professional Competence Commission for Malpractice Cases) established under Law no. 95/2006. This commission conducts an initial investigation and issues a report. If the findings support your claim or if you disagree with their conclusion, you may then pursue a civil lawsuit in court seeking damages. Our firm guides you through every stage, from gathering medical records to engaging independent medical experts.
faq.q3: What types of compensation can I receive in a medical malpractice case?
faq.a3: Romanian courts may award several categories of compensation: material damages covering medical expenses, rehabilitation costs, and lost income; moral damages (daune morale) for pain and suffering, emotional distress, and diminished quality of life; and future damages for ongoing medical care or permanent disability. The amount is determined by the court based on the severity of harm, the degree of negligence, and supporting evidence including expert medical reports.
faq.q4: How long does a medical malpractice case typically take in Romania?
faq.a4: Medical malpractice cases in Romania can be lengthy due to the complexity of medical evidence and court procedures. The initial complaint before the Malpractice Commission typically takes 3 to 6 months. If the case proceeds to court, litigation can take 1 to 3 years at first instance, with the possibility of appeal adding another 1 to 2 years. Our firm works diligently to expedite the process and keeps you informed at every stage.

drept-civil.description:
Civil law in Romania is governed by the Codul Civil (Civil Code), enacted through Legea nr. 287/2009 privind Codul Civil (Law no. 287/2009 on the Civil Code), which entered into force in 2011. This comprehensive legislation regulates the relationships between individuals and legal entities with respect to property rights, contractual obligations, civil liability (tort law), successions and inheritances, and real estate transactions. The Civil Code also incorporates provisions on prescription periods, evidence, and the enforcement of civil rights.

Our firm provides full-spectrum civil law services covering property disputes and land book (carte funciara) rectifications, contract drafting and negotiation, succession proceedings and partition of inherited assets, civil liability claims for material and moral damages, enforcement of court judgments (executare silita), and disputes regarding easements, boundary lines, and co-ownership. We represent clients before all levels of Romanian courts, from the Judecatorie (local court) to the Inalta Curte de Casatie si Justitie (High Court of Cassation and Justice).

For foreigners and English-speaking individuals involved in civil matters in Romania, whether purchasing property, resolving inheritance disputes, or pursuing damages, professional legal representation is indispensable. Romanian civil proceedings follow strict procedural rules under the Codul de Procedura Civila (Code of Civil Procedure), and all court documents, filings, and hearings are conducted exclusively in Romanian. Our bilingual attorneys ensure clear communication at every step, translate and explain legal documents, and advocate effectively on your behalf to protect your rights and interests.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How much does civil litigation cost in Romania?
faq.a1: The cost of civil litigation in Romania includes court fees (taxa judiciara de timbru), which are calculated based on the value of the claim and regulated by OUG nr. 80/2013. For property claims, the fee is a percentage of the claimed value (typically between 0.5% and 8%, on a sliding scale). Attorney fees vary depending on the complexity of the case. Our firm provides a transparent fee estimate during the initial consultation so you can make an informed decision before proceeding.
faq.q2: How long does a civil lawsuit take in Romania?
faq.a2: The duration of a civil case depends on its complexity, the court's workload, and the number of procedural steps involved. A straightforward civil claim at first instance (prima instanta) may take 6 to 18 months. If the losing party appeals (apel), an additional 6 to 12 months should be expected. Cases involving expert reports, multiple parties, or complex evidentiary issues may take longer. Our firm works to minimize delays through thorough preparation and proactive case management.
faq.q3: What documents are required to file a civil lawsuit in Romania?
faq.a3: To initiate a civil lawsuit (cerere de chemare in judecata), you generally need: proof of identity (identity card or passport), supporting evidence for your claim (contracts, correspondence, invoices, photos, witness statements), proof of payment of the court fee, and any prior correspondence or attempts at amicable resolution. For property-related claims, you will also need a land book extract (extras de carte funciara) and cadastral documentation. Our attorneys assist you in gathering and organizing all required documentation.
faq.q4: What is forced execution (executare silita) and how does it work?
faq.a4: Executare silita (forced execution) is the legal procedure through which a court judgment or other enforceable title is enforced against a debtor who fails to comply voluntarily. Under the Romanian Code of Civil Procedure, enforcement is carried out by a bailiff (executor judecatoresc) and may include seizure of bank accounts, garnishment of wages, seizure and sale of movable or immovable property, and eviction. The creditor must first obtain an enforceable title and file an enforcement request with a competent bailiff. Our firm assists clients throughout the enforcement process to ensure effective recovery of their rights.

drept-penal.description:
Criminal law in Romania is governed by the Codul Penal (Criminal Code), enacted through Legea nr. 286/2009 privind Codul Penal (Law no. 286/2009 on the Criminal Code), and the Codul de Procedura Penala (Code of Criminal Procedure), enacted through Legea nr. 135/2010. These laws define criminal offenses, penalties, the rights of suspects and defendants, and the procedural framework from criminal investigation through trial and appeals. Romanian criminal law classifies offenses by severity and provides for penalties ranging from fines to imprisonment.

Our firm provides comprehensive criminal defense services covering all categories of offenses: crimes against persons (assault, threats, homicide), crimes against property (theft, robbery, fraud, embezzlement), economic crimes and tax evasion, traffic offenses including driving under the influence, cybercrime, and corruption offenses. We represent both defendants and victims (parti civile) in criminal proceedings, ensuring that constitutional rights guaranteed under Art. 24 of the Romanian Constitution, including the right to defense, are fully protected at every procedural stage.

For foreign nationals and English speakers facing criminal charges or criminal investigations in Romania, having a skilled attorney is not just advisable but often legally required. Under Romanian law, legal representation is mandatory in serious cases involving potential imprisonment. All proceedings, from police interviews to court hearings, are conducted in Romanian, and procedural errors can have irreversible consequences. Our bilingual criminal defense attorneys provide immediate and confidential assistance, explain your rights clearly, and build a robust defense strategy tailored to your situation.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Do I have the right to a court-appointed lawyer in Romania?
faq.a1: Yes. Under the Romanian Code of Criminal Procedure and Art. 24 of the Constitution, every person has the right to defense. If you cannot afford a lawyer, the court will appoint one through the local Bar Association (Barou). Mandatory legal representation (asistenta juridica obligatorie) applies in cases where the suspect or defendant is a minor, is detained or arrested, the offense carries a penalty of more than 5 years imprisonment, or the person has certain vulnerabilities. However, a court-appointed lawyer may have limited time to dedicate to your case, which is why hiring a private attorney is strongly recommended for the most effective defense.
faq.q2: How long does a criminal trial take in Romania?
faq.a2: The duration of criminal proceedings varies significantly depending on the complexity of the case. The criminal investigation phase (urmarirea penala) conducted by prosecutors can take several months to over a year. Once the case reaches trial, first instance proceedings typically last 6 to 18 months. If either party appeals (apel), an additional 6 to 12 months is common. Complex cases involving multiple defendants, extensive evidence, or international cooperation may take considerably longer. Our firm works to protect your interests at every stage while pursuing the most favorable timeline.
faq.q3: What happens if I am detained or arrested in Romania?
faq.a3: If you are detained (retinere) by police, you can be held for a maximum of 24 hours without a court order. For continued deprivation of liberty, prosecutors must request preventive arrest (arestare preventiva) from a judge, who can order it for up to 30 days at a time, renewable up to a maximum of 180 days during investigation. You have the right to be informed of the charges, the right to remain silent, the right to an attorney (including a court-appointed one if needed), and the right to contact your embassy if you are a foreign national. It is critical to exercise your right to a lawyer immediately upon detention.
faq.q4: What is judicial control (control judiciar) in Romania?
faq.a4: Control judiciar (judicial control) is a preventive measure less restrictive than arrest, regulated by Art. 211-215 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Under judicial control, the suspect or defendant remains free but must comply with certain obligations, such as: not leaving the city or country without permission, reporting periodically to the police, not contacting certain persons (victims or witnesses), surrendering their passport, and other conditions set by the judge. Violating these obligations can result in the measure being replaced with house arrest or preventive arrest. Our attorneys can request judicial control as an alternative to arrest and help ensure compliance with its conditions.

drept-familiei.description:
Family law in Romania is regulated primarily by the Codul Civil (Civil Code), enacted through Legea nr. 287/2009, specifically Book II on Family (Cartea a II-a - Despre Familie), Articles 258-534. These provisions govern marriage, divorce, parent-child relationships, custody, child support (obligatia de intretinere), adoption, and guardianship. Additional procedural rules are found in the Codul de Procedura Civila (Code of Civil Procedure), and specific matters such as child protection are further regulated by Legea nr. 272/2004 privind protectia si promovarea drepturilor copilului (Law no. 272/2004 on the Protection and Promotion of Children's Rights).

Our firm handles the full spectrum of family law matters, including divorce by mutual consent (divort prin acordul sotilor) and contested divorce (divort din culpa), child custody arrangements and establishment of visitation schedules (program de vizitare), determination and modification of child support (pensie de intretinere), division of marital property (partaj bunuri comune), paternity recognition and contestation, and adoption and guardianship proceedings. We prioritize the best interests of children in all cases, as mandated by Art. 263 of the Civil Code.

For foreigners and English speakers involved in family law proceedings in Romania, whether through an international marriage, a cross-border custody dispute, or a divorce involving a Romanian spouse, legal representation is essential. Romanian family courts follow specific procedural requirements, and all filings and hearings are conducted in Romanian. Our bilingual attorneys provide compassionate, clear guidance through every stage, from mediation and notarial divorce to contested court proceedings, ensuring your rights and your children's welfare are fully protected.

A divorce by mutual consent (divort prin acordul sotilor) can be finalized before a notary public in as little as 30 days if there are no minor children and both parties agree on all terms. If minor children are involved, a mutual consent divorce is handled by the court and typically takes 2 to 4 months. A contested divorce (divort din culpa), where spouses disagree on fault, custody, or property division, can take 6 months to over 2 years depending on the complexity of the issues and the court's caseload.
faq.q2: How is child custody determined in Romania?
faq.a2: Under Art. 396-403 of the Romanian Civil Code, custody (autoritate parinteasca) is decided based on the best interests of the child. The court considers factors such as the child's age, emotional attachment to each parent, each parent's ability to provide stable living conditions, the child's own wishes (if the child is old enough to express a reasoned opinion, typically from age 10), and any history of domestic violence or neglect. The court may grant sole custody to one parent or joint custody (exercitarea in comun a autoritatii parintesti), which has become more common in recent years. The non-custodial parent retains visitation rights and the obligation to pay child support.
faq.q3: How is child support (pensie de intretinere) calculated in Romania?
faq.a3: Child support is regulated by Art. 529-530 of the Civil Code. The amount is set as a proportion of the paying parent's net monthly income: up to one-quarter (25%) for one child, up to one-third (33%) for two children, and up to one-half (50%) for three or more children. The court considers the actual needs of the child and the financial capacity of both parents. Child support can be modified if circumstances change significantly, such as a substantial increase or decrease in the paying parent's income, or changes in the child's needs.
faq.q4: Can I get a quick notarial divorce in Romania?
faq.a4: Yes, under Art. 375-378 of the Civil Code, spouses who agree on all terms of their divorce can finalize it before a notary public (notar public) if they have no minor children. The procedure involves a mandatory 30-day reflection period after the initial application. If there are minor children, even a mutual consent divorce must go through the court. The notarial divorce is significantly faster and less expensive than court proceedings, but both parties must fully agree on all aspects, including property division. Our firm can assist with preparing all necessary documents and ensuring the agreement protects your interests.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Can I be fired without cause in Romania?
faq.a1: No. Under the Romanian Labor Code (Codul Muncii), an employer cannot dismiss an employee without a valid legal ground. Lawful dismissal must be based on either reasons related to the employee (disciplinary misconduct, professional incompetence, or physical/mental incapacity) or reasons not related to the employee (elimination of the position due to economic, technological, or organizational restructuring). The employer must follow a strict procedural framework, including issuing a written dismissal decision (decizie de concediere) that specifies the factual and legal grounds. Dismissal without following proper procedure is considered unlawful and can be annulled by the court.
faq.q2: What is the notice period for termination in Romania?
faq.a2: Under Art. 75 of the Labor Code, the minimum notice period for employee resignation is 20 working days for non-managerial positions and 45 working days for managerial positions, unless a longer period is stipulated in the employment contract. For employer-initiated dismissal, the minimum notice period is also 20 working days, as provided by Art. 75 para. 1. During the notice period, the employment contract continues to produce its effects, meaning both the employee must work and the employer must pay the salary. Collective labor agreements or individual contracts may provide for longer notice periods.
faq.q3: Can I contest a dismissal in Romanian courts?
faq.a3: Yes. Under Art. 268 of the Labor Code, an employee can contest a dismissal decision before the Tribunal (labor disputes section) within 45 calendar days from the date they were notified of the dismissal decision. The burden of proof lies with the employer, who must demonstrate that the dismissal was lawful both in substance and procedure. If the court finds the dismissal unlawful, it can annul the dismissal decision, order reinstatement to the former position, and award compensation equal to the wages the employee would have earned from the date of dismissal until reinstatement. Employees are exempt from paying court fees in labor disputes.
faq.q4: What are my rights in a collective dismissal (concediere colectiva)?
faq.a4: Collective dismissal is regulated by Art. 68-74 of the Labor Code and occurs when an employer lays off a significant number of employees within 30 calendar days for economic, technological, or organizational reasons. The employer must follow a mandatory consultation procedure with trade unions or employee representatives, notify the Agentia Judeteana pentru Ocuparea Fortei de Munca (County Employment Agency) and the Inspectoratul Teritorial de Munca (Territorial Labor Inspectorate) at least 30 days before the layoffs take effect. Affected employees are entitled to the notice period, any severance pay provided by applicable collective agreements, and priority re-hiring if the employer fills similar positions within 45 days. Our firm can verify compliance with these procedural requirements and challenge unlawful collective dismissals.

faq.q1: What types of legal entities can I establish in Romania?
faq.a1: Under Legea nr. 31/1990 privind societatile (Company Law no. 31/1990), the most common types of legal entities in Romania are: SRL (Societate cu Raspundere Limitata) - a limited liability company, which is the most popular form for small and medium businesses, requiring a minimum share capital of 200 RON; SA (Societate pe Actiuni) - a joint-stock company, suitable for larger enterprises, requiring a minimum share capital of 90,000 RON; SNC (Societate in Nume Colectiv) - a general partnership; SCS (Societate in Comandita Simpla) - a limited partnership; and PFA (Persoana Fizica Autorizata) or II (Intreprindere Individuala) for sole traders. The choice depends on your business objectives, number of partners, capital requirements, and liability preferences.
faq.q2: How much does it cost to form a company in Romania?
faq.a2: The cost of forming an SRL (the most common business entity) in Romania includes: the minimum share capital of 200 RON (approximately 40 EUR), Trade Register fees of approximately 100-300 RON, notarial fees for authenticating the articles of incorporation, publication fees in the Monitorul Oficial (Official Gazette), and attorney fees for legal assistance with drafting documents and handling the registration process. Total costs typically range from 1,500 to 3,000 RON (300-600 EUR) including professional fees. The registration process at the Oficiul Registrului Comertului (Trade Register Office) usually takes 3 to 5 business days once all documents are submitted.
faq.q3: What is insolvency and how does it work in Romania?
faq.a3: Insolvency in Romania is regulated by Legea nr. 85/2014 privind procedurile de prevenire a insolventei si de insolventa (Law no. 85/2014 on Insolvency Prevention and Insolvency Procedures). A company is considered insolvent when it cannot pay its debts as they fall due. The law provides for several procedures: preventive composition (concordatul preventiv), judicial reorganization (reorganizare judiciara), which allows the company to restructure its debts and continue operations under a reorganization plan, and bankruptcy (faliment), which involves liquidation of assets and distribution of proceeds to creditors. Insolvency proceedings are initiated before the Tribunal and managed by a judicial administrator (administrator judiciar) or liquidator (lichidator judiciar). Both debtors and creditors can file insolvency petitions.
faq.q4: How can I recover a commercial debt in Romania?
faq.a4: Romanian law provides several mechanisms for debt recovery. For undisputed debts, you can use the ordonanta de plata (payment order) procedure under Art. 1014-1025 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which provides an expedited resolution within approximately 45 days. For debts evidenced by specific documents (invoices, contracts), the cerere cu valoare redusa (small claims procedure) may apply for claims under 10,000 EUR. If the debt is disputed, standard civil litigation is required. After obtaining an enforceable title (court judgment or payment order), forced execution (executare silita) is carried out by a bailiff (executor judecatoresc) and may include bank account seizure, wage garnishment, and seizure of assets. Our firm handles the entire recovery process from pre-litigation demand letters to enforcement.

faq.q1: What should I do immediately after a traffic accident in Romania?

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is administrative litigation in Romania?
faq.a1: Administrative litigation (contencios administrativ) is the legal mechanism through which individuals and legal entities can challenge unlawful acts issued by public authorities. It is primarily governed by Legea nr. 554/2004 privind contenciosul administrativ (Law no. 554/2004 on Administrative Disputes). Under this law, any person who considers that a right or legitimate interest has been harmed by an administrative act - or by the failure of an authority to resolve a request within the legal deadline - may bring an action before the administrative courts. Before filing suit, the injured party must generally submit a prior administrative complaint (plangere prealabila) to the issuing authority under Art. 7 of Law no. 554/2004, requesting revocation or modification of the act. If the authority rejects the complaint or fails to respond within 30 days, the person may then file an action in the competent administrative and fiscal court (tribunal - sectia de contencios administrativ si fiscal). The court can annul the administrative act, order the authority to issue a new act, and award damages for the harm suffered.
faq.q2: How do I challenge a tax assessment from ANAF?
faq.a2: To challenge a tax assessment decision (decizie de impunere) issued by ANAF (Agentia Nationala de Administrare Fiscala - National Agency for Fiscal Administration), you must first file a fiscal appeal (contestatie fiscala) under Art. 268-281 of the Codul de Procedura Fiscala (Tax Procedure Code, Legea nr. 207/2015 privind Codul de Procedura Fiscala). The appeal must be filed in writing with the issuing tax authority within 45 days from the date of communication of the decision, as provided by Art. 270. The issuing authority forwards the file to the competent resolution body - the Directia Generala de Solutionare a Contestatiilor (General Directorate for Resolving Appeals) within ANAF for amounts exceeding 5 million RON, or the relevant regional fiscal authority for smaller amounts. The resolution body must issue a decision within 45 days (extendable to 6 months for complex cases). If your fiscal appeal is rejected in whole or in part, you may then challenge the decision before the administrative and fiscal court under Legea nr. 554/2004 within 6 months from communication of the appellate decision.
faq.q3: What is the deadline for challenging an administrative act?
faq.a3: Under Art. 11 of Legea nr. 554/2004 privind contenciosul administrativ (Law no. 554/2004 on Administrative Disputes), the action in administrative litigation must be filed within 6 months from the date of communication of the authority's response to the prior complaint (plangere prealabila), or from the date when the legal deadline for the authority to respond has expired without a reply. There is also an absolute limitation period of 1 year from the date of communication of the administrative act itself, beyond which the right to challenge is lost regardless of circumstances. For tax matters specifically, the fiscal appeal under Art. 270 of the Tax Procedure Code (Legea nr. 207/2015) must be filed within 45 days from communication of the tax assessment decision. These deadlines are mandatory and their expiration extinguishes the right to bring an action, which is why it is critical to consult a specialized attorney immediately upon receiving an unfavorable administrative or tax decision.
faq.q4: Can I obtain suspension of an administrative act's enforcement?
faq.a4: Yes, under Art. 14-15 of Legea nr. 554/2004 privind contenciosul administrativ (Law no. 554/2004 on Administrative Disputes), the injured party may request the court to suspend the enforcement of an administrative act. To obtain suspension, two cumulative conditions must be met: the existence of a well-founded case (caz bine justificat), meaning serious arguments suggesting the administrative act may be unlawful, and the risk of imminent damage (paguba iminenta) - harm of a certain degree that cannot be remedied if the act continues to produce effects. Suspension can be requested either together with the prior complaint (Art. 14, decided by the court without the main action being filed yet) or alongside the main action for annulment (Art. 15). The court may require the applicant to post a security deposit (cautiune). In tax matters, filing a fiscal appeal (contestatie fiscala) does not automatically suspend enforcement under Art. 278 of the Tax Procedure Code, but the court may grant suspension under the same conditions of Art. 14-15 of Law no. 554/2004. Our attorneys evaluate the strength of your case, prepare the suspension request with supporting evidence, and represent you in the urgent hearing before the administrative court.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is CNSC and what role does it play in public procurement?
faq.a1: CNSC (Consiliul National de Solutionare a Contestatiilor - National Council for Solving Complaints) is Romania's specialized administrative-jurisdictional body that resolves complaints in public procurement matters. Established under Legea nr. 101/2016 privind remediile si caile de atac (Law no. 101/2016 on Remedies and Appeals), CNSC has exclusive competence to review complaints filed by economic operators who consider that their rights have been violated during a procurement procedure. CNSC must issue a decision within 20 days of receiving the complete file, and its decisions can be appealed before the competent court of appeal within 10 days from communication.
faq.q2: What are the deadlines for filing a complaint in public procurement?
faq.a2: Under Legea nr. 101/2016 privind remediile si caile de atac (Law no. 101/2016 on Remedies and Appeals), the deadline for filing a complaint before CNSC depends on the estimated contract value. For contracts above the EU thresholds, the complaint must be filed within 10 days from the date when the complainant became aware of the act considered unlawful. For contracts below the EU thresholds, the deadline is 5 days. These deadlines are mandatory and their non-observance leads to the rejection of the complaint as belated. Prior notification of the contracting authority under Art. 6 of Law 101/2016 is also required before filing with CNSC.
faq.q3: Can I challenge an exclusion from a tender procedure?
faq.a3: Yes, an economic operator excluded from a public procurement procedure has the right to challenge the exclusion decision before CNSC or directly before the competent court. Under Legea nr. 98/2016 (Law no. 98/2016 on Public Procurement), exclusion must be based on specific grounds enumerated in Art. 164-167, including criminal convictions, tax debts, or serious professional misconduct. If the contracting authority applied the exclusion grounds incorrectly, failed to allow the operator to provide clarifications, or did not properly apply the self-cleaning mechanism under Art. 171, the decision may be annulled. Our attorneys carefully review the exclusion reasoning and prepare a well-founded complaint to protect your right to participate.
faq.q4: Can I claim damages for an unlawful procurement decision?
faq.a4: Yes, under Art. 53 of Legea nr. 101/2016 privind remediile si caile de atac (Law no. 101/2016 on Remedies and Appeals), any person who has suffered harm as a result of an unlawful act or decision during a procurement procedure may seek damages before the competent court. To succeed, the claimant must prove the unlawfulness of the contracting authority's act, the actual damage suffered (including lost profit from not being awarded the contract), and the causal link between the two. The claim must be filed within the general civil statute of limitations of three years. Our firm assists with quantifying the damages, gathering evidence, and representing clients in court to recover compensation.

drept-contraventional.description:
Contravention law in Romania is primarily governed by OG nr. 2/2001 privind regimul juridic al contraventiilor (Government Ordinance no. 2/2001 on the Legal Regime of Contraventions), which establishes the general framework for defining contraventions, applying sanctions, and challenging contravention reports. A contravention (contraventie) is a deed committed with guilt, established and sanctioned by law, ordinance, or local council decision, distinct from criminal offenses by its lower degree of social danger. Sanctions range from warnings (avertisment) to fines (amenda) and complementary sanctions such as confiscation or suspension of activity.

Our firm specializes in challenging contravention reports (procese-verbale de constatare si sanctionare a contraventiei) before Romanian courts. Under Art. 31 of OG 2/2001, the sanctioned person has the right to file a complaint (plangere contraventionala) within 15 days from the date of communication of the report. The complaint is filed with the judecatorie (local court) in whose jurisdiction the contravention was committed. The court examines both the legality and the merits of the report, and may annul it, reduce the fine, or replace it with a warning. Importantly, under ECHR case-law applied by Romanian courts, contravention proceedings must respect fair trial guarantees, including the presumption of innocence.

For foreign nationals and English speakers who receive contravention fines in Romania - whether for traffic violations, construction irregularities, or commercial activities - understanding your rights is crucial. Many contravention reports contain procedural defects that may lead to annulment, such as failure to properly identify the person sanctioned, incorrect legal classification, or failure to describe the deed with sufficient precision. Our bilingual attorneys review the report for both formal and substantive defects, prepare the legal complaint within the 15-day deadline, and represent you before the competent court to ensure the best possible outcome.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is the deadline for challenging a contravention fine in Romania?
faq.a1: Under Art. 31 of OG nr. 2/2001 privind regimul juridic al contraventiilor (Government Ordinance no. 2/2001 on the Legal Regime of Contraventions), the person sanctioned must file a complaint (plangere contraventionala) within 15 days from the date of communication or receipt of the contravention report (proces-verbal). The complaint is filed with the judecatorie (local court) in whose jurisdiction the contravention was committed. This deadline is mandatory, and failure to file within 15 days results in the report becoming final and enforceable. If you have received a fine, it is essential to contact an attorney immediately to preserve your right to challenge.
faq.q2: What aspects of a contravention report can be challenged?
faq.a2: A contravention report can be challenged on both legality (legalitate) and merits (temeinicie). On legality grounds, the court verifies whether the report contains all mandatory elements required by Art. 16-17 of OG 2/2001, such as correct identification of the sanctioned person, precise description of the deed, legal classification, and the agent's signature. Absence of these elements may lead to absolute nullity. On the merits, the court examines whether the deed was actually committed, whether it constitutes a contravention, and whether the sanction applied is proportionate. Romanian courts also apply ECHR principles, including the presumption of innocence, meaning the burden of proof rests with the sanctioning authority.
faq.q3: What happens if I do not pay a contravention fine?
faq.a3: If the contravention report becomes final (either because the 15-day challenge period expired or the court rejected the complaint), the fine becomes enforceable. Under OG 2/2001 and the Codul de Procedura Fiscala (Tax Procedure Code), unpaid fines are collected through forced execution (executare silita) by ANAF or local tax authorities. This may involve garnishment of bank accounts, seizure of income, or seizure of movable and immovable property. Additionally, under Art. 28 of OG 2/2001, if the fine is paid within 15 days from communication, the sanctioned person benefits from paying only half of the minimum fine amount. For foreign nationals, unpaid fines may also affect future visa or residence applications in Romania.
faq.q4: Can a contravention fine be replaced with a warning?
faq.a4: Yes, under Art. 7 of OG nr. 2/2001, the warning (avertisment) is the mildest contravention sanction and can be applied when the deed is of minor gravity. If the sanctioning agent applied a fine, the court hearing the complaint may replace it with a warning if it considers that the circumstances justify a milder sanction, taking into account the nature and gravity of the deed, the circumstances of its commission, the person's conduct, and whether any harm was caused. Romanian courts frequently apply the proportionality principle and replace disproportionate fines with warnings, particularly for first-time offenders and minor violations. Our attorneys present all mitigating factors to maximize the chances of obtaining a warning instead of a fine.

dreptul-asigurarilor.description:
Insurance law in Romania is governed by Legea nr. 132/2017 privind asigurarea obligatorie de raspundere civila auto (Law no. 132/2017 on Mandatory Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance - RCA), the Codul Civil (Civil Code) provisions on insurance contracts (Art. 2199-2242), and ASF (Autoritatea de Supraveghere Financiara - Financial Supervisory Authority) regulations. The insurance framework covers mandatory motor vehicle liability insurance (RCA), optional comprehensive insurance (CASCO), life insurance, property insurance, professional liability insurance, and various other insurance products. ASF supervises and regulates the insurance market to ensure consumer protection and market stability.

Our firm handles the full spectrum of insurance disputes, from filing initial damage claims to representing clients in court against insurance companies that refuse or undervalue compensation. We assist clients with RCA claims following traffic accidents, including obtaining fair compensation for vehicle repairs, medical expenses, lost income, and moral damages. For CASCO policyholders, we challenge unjustified claim denials and underpayments. We also represent beneficiaries in life insurance disputes, property insurance claims following natural disasters or other covered events, and professional liability insurance matters. Our experience with ASF complaint procedures provides an additional avenue for resolving disputes before resorting to litigation.

For foreigners and English speakers involved in insurance matters in Romania - particularly traffic accident claims under the RCA system - understanding local procedures is essential. Romania's insurance claim process involves strict notification deadlines, mandatory damage assessment procedures (constatare amiabila de accident or police reports), and specific documentation requirements. Insurance companies frequently attempt to minimize payouts or invoke technical exclusions. Our bilingual attorneys ensure you receive the full compensation you are entitled to under Romanian law, handling all communication with the insurer, arranging independent damage assessments, and pursuing court action when the insurer fails to offer a fair settlement.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is the deadline for filing an insurance claim in Romania?
faq.a1: The deadline for filing an insurance claim depends on the type of insurance. For RCA (mandatory motor vehicle liability insurance) under Legea nr. 132/2017, the injured party must notify the insurer within a reasonable time, and the insurer must respond with a compensation offer or reasoned rejection within 30 days from the date the complete file was submitted (or 90 days for bodily injury claims requiring medical assessment). The general civil statute of limitations for insurance claims under Art. 2517 of the Codul Civil is three years from the date the insured event occurred or when the insured became aware of the damage. For CASCO policies, the notification deadline is typically specified in the policy terms, usually 24-48 hours for theft and 5-7 days for other events. Missing these deadlines can jeopardize your right to compensation.
faq.q2: What can I do if the insurance company refuses my claim?
faq.a2: If an insurance company refuses your claim or offers insufficient compensation, you have several legal options. First, you may file a complaint with ASF (Autoritatea de Supraveghere Financiara - Financial Supervisory Authority), which supervises the insurance market and can sanction insurers for unfair practices. Second, you may pursue mediation or the SAL-Fin (Entitatea de Solutionare Alternativa a Litigiilor in Domeniul Financiar-Nebancar) alternative dispute resolution procedure. Third and most effectively, you may file a civil lawsuit against the insurer before the competent Romanian court, seeking full compensation plus legal interest from the date the payment was due. Romanian courts have consistently awarded damages exceeding insurer offers, particularly in bodily injury cases. Our attorneys evaluate the insurer's refusal, gather independent expert evidence, and pursue the most effective legal strategy.
faq.q3: What is the difference between RCA and CASCO insurance?
faq.a3: RCA (asigurare obligatorie de raspundere civila auto - mandatory motor vehicle liability insurance) is compulsory for all vehicle owners in Romania under Legea nr. 132/2017. It covers damages caused by the insured vehicle to third parties, including bodily injuries, property damage, and moral damages. The injured third party can claim directly against the at-fault driver's RCA insurer. CASCO (asigurare auto comprehensiva) is a voluntary comprehensive insurance that covers damage to the policyholder's own vehicle, regardless of fault, including theft, natural disasters, vandalism, and accidents. While RCA protects third-party victims, CASCO protects the vehicle owner. In practice, after a traffic accident, the victim claims from the at-fault party's RCA, while the at-fault party may claim from their own CASCO for their vehicle damage.
faq.q4: Can I claim moral damages (daune morale) from an insurance company?
faq.a4: Yes, moral damages (daune morale) are recoverable in insurance claims under Romanian law, particularly in cases involving bodily injuries or death resulting from traffic accidents covered by RCA insurance. Under Legea nr. 132/2017 and the Codul Civil provisions on civil liability, the insurer must compensate not only material damages but also non-patrimonial harm including physical suffering, emotional distress, loss of quality of life, and loss of consortium. Romanian courts have developed a substantial body of case-law on quantifying moral damages, considering factors such as severity of injuries, duration of suffering, permanent disability, age of the victim, and impact on daily life. Awards for moral damages in serious injury cases can reach significant amounts. Our firm works with medical experts to document the full extent of harm suffered and presents compelling arguments to maximize the moral damages awarded.

practician-insolventa.description:
Insolvency law in Romania is governed by Legea nr. 85/2014 privind procedurile de prevenire a insolventei si de insolventa (Law no. 85/2014 on Insolvency Prevention and Insolvency Proceedings). Under Art. 5 pct. 29 of this law, insolvency is defined as the state of the debtor's patrimony characterized by insufficient available funds to pay certain, liquid, and due debts. The law provides two main procedural paths: the general procedure (procedura generala), which includes an observation period, judicial reorganization, and potentially bankruptcy (faliment), and the simplified procedure (procedura simplificata), which leads directly to bankruptcy for debtors who do not meet the criteria for reorganization.

Our firm provides full legal assistance to both debtors and creditors throughout all stages of insolvency proceedings. For debtor companies facing financial difficulty, we advise on the option of filing a voluntary insolvency petition, assist with the preparation and implementation of reorganization plans (plan de reorganizare) aimed at restructuring debts and continuing business operations, and represent the debtor before the syndic judge (judecator-sindic) and the creditors' assembly (adunarea creditorilor). For creditors, we handle the registration of claims (declaratii de creanta) within the legal deadlines, challenge the preliminary and final tables of claims (tabel preliminar si tabel definitiv de creante), and pursue recovery of debts through the insolvency procedure.

For foreign creditors or international companies with exposure to Romanian debtors in insolvency, understanding the Romanian insolvency framework is critical for protecting your interests. The claims registration deadline under Art. 100 of Legea nr. 85/2014 is strict and typically set at 45 days from the opening of proceedings, with failure to register resulting in forfeiture of the right to participate in distributions. Our bilingual team assists foreign creditors with preparing and filing claims, attending creditors' meetings, challenging the insolvency practitioner's decisions, and pursuing all available remedies to maximize recovery. We also advise on cross-border insolvency matters and the recognition of foreign insolvency proceedings under EU Regulation 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings.

cases.case2: Drafting and implementing judicial reorganization plans

approach.point4: We monitor the entire insolvency procedure and pursue maximum recovery for creditors or optimal restructuring for debtors.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is the legal definition of insolvency in Romania?
faq.a1: Under Art. 5 pct. 29 of Legea nr. 85/2014 privind procedurile de prevenire a insolventei si de insolventa (Law no. 85/2014 on Insolvency Prevention and Insolvency Proceedings), insolvency is defined as the state of the debtor's patrimony characterized by insufficient available funds to pay certain, liquid, and due debts (datorii certe, lichide si exigibile). Insolvency is presumed when the debtor has not paid its debt within 60 days of the due date. There is also the concept of imminent insolvency (insolventa iminenta) under Art. 5 pct. 30, when the debtor proves that it will not be able to pay its debts as they fall due. The minimum threshold for opening insolvency proceedings is a claim of at least 50,000 RON (approximately EUR 10,000). A debtor may also voluntarily file for insolvency when it anticipates inability to pay debts.
faq.q2: What is the difference between judicial reorganization and liquidation (bankruptcy)?
faq.a2: Judicial reorganization (reorganizare judiciara) and liquidation/bankruptcy (faliment) represent two distinct phases of insolvency proceedings under Legea nr. 85/2014. Reorganization is a rescue procedure aimed at enabling the debtor to continue its business activities while restructuring its debts according to a reorganization plan approved by creditors and confirmed by the syndic judge. The plan may involve debt rescheduling, partial debt write-offs, operational restructuring, or sale of assets. If reorganization succeeds, the debtor emerges from insolvency as a viable business. Liquidation (bankruptcy) occurs when reorganization fails or is not feasible, and involves the sale of the debtor's assets to pay creditors according to the order of priority established by Art. 159 of the law, followed by dissolution of the company. The general insolvency procedure allows for both stages, while the simplified procedure leads directly to bankruptcy.
faq.q3: What is the deadline for registering creditor claims?
faq.a3: Under Art. 100 alin. (1) of Legea nr. 85/2014, creditors must file their claims (declaratii de creanta) with the insolvency court and the insolvency practitioner within the deadline established by the syndic judge in the judgment opening the insolvency proceedings, which is typically 45 days from the date of the opening decision. Late claims can still be registered under Art. 100 alin. (4) up until the final date for establishing the updated table of claims, but late-filing creditors lose the right to challenge the preliminary table, to vote on the reorganization plan, and to participate in distributions made prior to their registration. Complete failure to register results in forfeiture of the claim against the insolvent debtor. Given these severe consequences, it is critical to monitor the Buletinul Procedurilor de Insolventa (Insolvency Proceedings Bulletin) and register claims promptly.
faq.q4: Can directors be held personally liable in insolvency?
faq.a4: Yes, under Art. 169 of Legea nr. 85/2014, the syndic judge may order members of the management or supervisory bodies (directors, board members, shareholders with control) to bear personal liability for part or all of the debtor's outstanding debts if their actions contributed to the company's insolvency. Grounds for personal liability include: using the company's assets for personal benefit, conducting fictitious commercial activities, continuing business operations when insolvency was inevitable in order to increase the state of insolvency, keeping fictitious or incomplete accounting records, misappropriating or concealing company assets, and using ruinous methods to obtain funds to delay insolvency. The action for personal liability can be brought by the insolvency practitioner, the creditors' committee, or creditors holding at least 50% of the total claims. The amounts recovered through personal liability increase the funds available for distribution to creditors.

arbitraj-intern.description:
Domestic arbitration in Romania is regulated by the Codul de Procedura Civila (Code of Civil Procedure), specifically Art. 541-621 under Book IV on Arbitration. Arbitration is a private, alternative method of resolving disputes in which the parties agree to submit their conflict to one or more arbitrators rather than to state courts. The arbitration agreement (conventia arbitrala) may take the form of an arbitration clause (clauza compromisorie) included in a contract, or a separate submission agreement (compromis) concluded after the dispute has arisen. Romania also hosts institutional arbitration through the Curtea de Arbitraj Comercial International de pe langa Camera de Comert si Industrie a Romaniei (Court of International Commercial Arbitration attached to the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Romania).

Our firm provides comprehensive arbitration services, from drafting effective arbitration clauses in commercial contracts to representing clients throughout the entire arbitration proceedings. We handle both ad-hoc arbitration governed directly by the Civil Procedure Code and institutional arbitration conducted under the rules of established arbitration institutions. Additionally, we advise on and represent clients in mediation proceedings under Legea nr. 192/2006 privind medierea si organizarea profesiei de mediator (Law no. 192/2006 on Mediation and the Organization of the Mediator Profession), which provides a flexible, confidential, and cost-effective method of dispute resolution that can be used independently or in conjunction with arbitration.

For foreign companies and English-speaking individuals involved in commercial disputes in Romania, arbitration offers significant advantages over traditional litigation: faster resolution (typically 6-12 months versus 2-5 years in courts), confidentiality of proceedings, flexibility in choosing applicable rules and language, and the enforceability of arbitral awards under the New York Convention for international disputes. Our bilingual team assists international clients with selecting appropriate arbitration forums, negotiating arbitration agreements, preparing and presenting their case before the arbitral tribunal, and enforcing or challenging arbitral awards under Art. 608-613 of the Civil Procedure Code. We also represent foreign parties in mediation sessions conducted in English or Romanian.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is the difference between arbitration and litigation in Romania?
faq.a1: Arbitration and litigation are two distinct methods of resolving disputes. Litigation is conducted before Romanian state courts (judecatorie, tribunal, curtea de apel, Inalta Curte de Casatie si Justitie) under the Codul de Procedura Civila, with proceedings open to the public, strict procedural rules, and the possibility of multiple levels of appeal. Arbitration, governed by Art. 541-621 of the same Code, is a private mechanism where the parties choose one or more arbitrators to decide their dispute. Key differences include speed (arbitration typically resolves in 6-12 months versus 2-5 years for litigation), confidentiality (arbitration proceedings are private), flexibility (parties can choose procedural rules and language), and finality (arbitral awards are generally not subject to appeal on the merits, only to annulment for limited procedural grounds under Art. 608 CPC). However, arbitration requires an agreement between the parties and is generally limited to patrimonial disputes that can be subject to a settlement.
faq.q2: Are arbitral awards enforceable in Romania?
faq.a2: Yes, arbitral awards are fully enforceable in Romania. Under Art. 615 of the Codul de Procedura Civila, a domestic arbitral award that is no longer subject to annulment constitutes an enforceable title (titlu executoriu) and can be enforced through forced execution just like a court judgment. For enforcement, the party must obtain an executory formula (incuviintarea executarii silite) from the competent court. International arbitral awards rendered abroad are recognized and enforced in Romania under the 1958 New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards, to which Romania is a signatory, as well as under Art. 1123-1132 of the Civil Procedure Code. The Romanian court may only refuse recognition or enforcement on narrow grounds specified in the New York Convention, such as invalidity of the arbitration agreement, violation of due process, or public policy concerns.
faq.q3: On what grounds can an arbitral award be challenged?
faq.a3: Under Art. 608 of the Codul de Procedura Civila, an arbitral award can be challenged through an action for annulment (actiune in anulare) filed before the competent court of appeal within one month from communication of the award. The grounds for annulment are strictly limited and include: the dispute was not capable of being resolved through arbitration; the arbitral tribunal was constituted in violation of the arbitration agreement; the award was rendered after the expiry of the arbitration term; the tribunal ruled on matters not submitted to it (ultra petita) or failed to rule on a submitted matter; the award violates public policy, good morals, or mandatory legal provisions; and the award does not contain the required elements under Art. 603 CPC. Importantly, the court reviewing the annulment action does not re-examine the merits of the dispute but only verifies whether the procedural grounds for annulment are met. Our attorneys carefully analyze the award and advise on the viability and strategy of any annulment action.
faq.q4: What is mediation and when is it recommended?
faq.a4: Mediation in Romania is governed by Legea nr. 192/2006 privind medierea si organizarea profesiei de mediator (Law no. 192/2006 on Mediation and the Organization of the Mediator Profession). It is a voluntary, confidential process in which a neutral, trained mediator facilitates communication between the parties to help them reach a mutually acceptable agreement. Unlike arbitration or litigation, the mediator does not impose a decision - the parties retain full control over the outcome. Mediation is particularly recommended for disputes where the parties wish to preserve their business relationship, when confidentiality is important, when a creative solution beyond what a court could order is desired, or when speed and cost-efficiency are priorities. Under Romanian law, for certain types of disputes (including commercial disputes above 50,000 RON), parties are required to attend an informative mediation session before filing a court action, although actual participation in mediation remains voluntary. A mediation agreement has the legal force of a contract between the parties and can be authenticated by a notary to become an enforceable title.

introduction.title: 1. Introduction
introduction.content: Stan-Baculescu Law Firm (hereinafter referred to as "the Firm", "we" or "our") uses cookies and similar technologies on our website to provide you with an optimal browsing experience, to analyze site traffic, and to personalize content. This Cookie Policy explains what cookies are, what types of cookies we use, and how you can manage them.

whatAreCookies.title: 2. What Are Cookies?
whatAreCookies.content: Cookies are small text files that are placed on your device (computer, tablet, mobile phone) when you visit a website. They allow the site to recognize your device and store information about your preferences or previous actions. Cookies do not contain directly identifiable personal information and cannot access or damage your device.

essentialCookies.title: 3. Essential Cookies
essentialCookies.content: These cookies are strictly necessary for our website to function and cannot be disabled. They are set in response to your actions, such as setting privacy preferences or selecting language. Without these cookies, the site cannot function properly.

cookieConsent.purpose: Stores your consent for the use of cookies

cookiePreferences.purpose: Stores your preferences for cookie categories

analyticsCookies.title: 4. Analytics Cookies
analyticsCookies.content: These cookies allow us to measure and analyze how visitors interact with our website. They help us understand which pages are most popular, how visitors navigate the site, and if they encounter errors. All data collected by these cookies is aggregated and anonymous. We use Google Tag Manager (GTM) for script management and Google Analytics 4 (GA4) for traffic analysis.

ga.purpose: Used by Google Analytics to distinguish unique users

gaId.purpose: Used by Google Analytics to maintain session state

gid.purpose: Used by Google Analytics to distinguish unique users throughout a single day

marketingCookies.title: 5. Marketing Cookies
marketingCookies.content: These cookies are used to display relevant advertisements and to measure the effectiveness of advertising campaigns. They are only activated with your explicit consent. Currently, we use Facebook Pixel (Meta) in this category.

fbp.purpose: Used by Facebook/Meta Pixel to identify the browser for displaying relevant advertisements

fbc.purpose: Stores the click identifier from Facebook ads for conversion measurement

thirdPartyServices.title: 6. Technologies and Third-Party Services
thirdPartyServices.content: In addition to cookies, our website uses the following third-party services for operation and improvement:

items.item1: Google Tag Manager (GTM) — a tag management system that allows us to manage scripts on the site. GTM does not set its own cookies and does not directly collect personal data, but it facilitates the loading of other services (Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel) that may set cookies.
items.item2: Vercel — the hosting platform on which our website is hosted. Vercel does not set tracking cookies on your device. Technical data necessary for delivering web pages (IP address, user agent) is processed transiently according to Vercel Inc.'s privacy policy.
items.item3: Resend — the transactional email service we use to process messages sent through the contact form. Resend does not set cookies on our website. Form data (name, email, message) is transmitted to Resend's servers for email delivery, in accordance with the data processing agreement entered into with this provider.

manageCookies.title: 7. How to Manage Cookies
manageCookies.content: You have full control over the cookies you accept. You can manage your preferences in the following ways:

items.item1: Through the consent banner: On your first visit to the site, a banner is displayed allowing you to accept all cookies, reject non-essential ones, or customize your choice.
items.item2: Through cookie settings: You can access cookie settings at any time from the website footer to change your preferences.
items.item3: Through browser settings: Most browsers allow you to block or delete cookies. Consult your browser's help section for instructions.
items.item4: Important: Disabling essential cookies may affect the proper functioning of our website.

retention.title: 8. Retention Period
retention.content: Essential and preference cookies are stored for 1 year. Analytics cookies (Google Analytics) are stored for 2 years. Marketing cookies (Facebook Pixel) are stored between 3 months and 2 years, depending on the cookie type. You can delete cookies at any time from your browser settings or by revoking consent through the cookie settings on our website.
